summary:
I fixed all five issues the verifier raised: the major one and the four minor ones. I also fixed one of the verifier's two side observations (the race in the "rendered" report). Every suite passes on this machine.

**Final test runs**
- core: 15 tests pass.
- webview: type-check, build, 24 unit tests and 13 Playwright tests in Chrome pass. The Playwright suite also passed when repeated (26 of 26).
- extension: 4 unit tests and 5 smoke tests inside VS Code 1.140.0 under xvfb pass. The smoke suite passed on all 3 runs.

**What changed**
1. **Contributed colours (major).** VS Code turns a colour id into a CSS variable by replacing only its first dot, so ids with two dots never reached the board. I renamed the ids to one dot each: `telelean.kindAssumption`, `telelean.kindDerivation`, `telelean.kindGoal` and `telelean.formalizedAura`. `board.css` now reads the variables VS Code actually sets. Three new tests check this:
   - a static test that compares the manifest with the CSS;
   - a Playwright test that uses VS Code's naming rule;
   - a smoke test that sets `workbench.colorCustomizations` in the test instance's own profile. Inside real VS Code the board then showed aura `rgb(255, 0, 255)`, and a formalised card's glow used that colour.
2. **CSP violations during page load.** A small classic script, `boot.js`, now loads with the nonce before the stylesheet. It records any violation and hands it to the bundle once the bundle starts. The "rendered" report now also says whether the stylesheet applied, and smoke test 2 checks this. I repeated the verifier's blocked-stylesheet probe in a scratch copy: test 2 now fails ("styled false, column heights 144,18,36"), and the host log shows the `csp-violation` just before `ready`.
3. **Protocol.** The host-side check now rejects:
   - a kind change to the same kind, or one that places a card before itself;
   - repeated ids in `select` or in the premises of `theseSuffice`;
   - a `__proto__` key, or a key longer than 64 characters, in diagnostic data.
4. **Visual polish.**
   - The "▲ n linked" button now sits in each column's header and "▼ n linked" in a new 24 px footer, so neither covers a card. A Playwright test checks where they sit, that their counts are right, and that clicking one scrolls only its own column.
   - An empty column shows an opaque placeholder centred in the column, so arrows no longer run through its text.
5. **Chrome temp files.** Each Playwright run gives Chrome its own short temp folder and deletes it at the end. This works even when TMPDIR is the long scratchpad path, which used to stop Chrome from starting. No new `/tmp/com.google.Chrome.*` folders appeared.
6. **"rendered" race (verifier's side observation).** The report is now tied to the graph it describes, and a report for a graph that has been replaced is dropped. With that check removed in a scratch copy, the new test failed 3 out of 3: one report was labelled graph #2 but counted graph #3's cards.

**Things you should know**
- **I briefly wrote outside my assigned paths, and cleaned it up.** A mistake in one of my shell commands launched Playwright from the repo root. It created `/home/zhengyew/telelean/test-results/.last-run.json` (created at 07:59:52, status "failed"). I deleted that folder. No other repo file changed in that time window; the runner files changed since 07:42 belong to other agents and changed at other times.
- **The colour ids now differ from the example in 03 §7**, which names `telelean.node.formalizedAura`. I am not allowed to edit the design docs.
- **The test profile in the real repo uses the Abyss theme.** I don't know how it got that way. A fresh profile uses "Dark 2026". In Abyss, the Goal colour comes out translucent grey (details in not_fixed).
- **My colour smoke test leaves a `{}` settings.json** in `/home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/extension/.vscode-test/user-data/User/`. That is the test instance's profile, not yours.

**Rules kept:** `~/.elan/known-projects` still has 36 lines, your VS Code settings are unchanged (last modified 2026-08-28), and telelean is not installed in your VS Code. There were no installs, no Claude CLI runs and no git commands, and nothing of mine is still running.

**Files**, all under `/home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/`:
- core: `src/protocol.ts`, `test/protocol.test.ts`
- webview, new: `public/boot.js`, `test/harness/chrome-tmp.ts`, `test/harness/blocked-style.html`, `test/shared/vscode-theme.ts`, `test/unit/theme.test.ts`
- webview, changed:
  - source: `src/host/bridge.ts`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/board/{diagnostics.ts,Board.tsx,Column.tsx,EdgeEngine.ts,geometry.ts}`, `src/state/store.ts`, `src/styles/board.css`
  - config: `vite.config.ts` (a comment only), `playwright.config.ts`
  - tests: `test/harness/{index.html,harness.js}`, `test/unit/geometry.test.ts`, `test/e2e/{board.spec.ts,helpers.ts}`
  - screenshots, regenerated: `test-results/*.png`
- extension: `package.json` (colour ids), `src/board/{html.ts,BoardPanel.ts}`, `test/unit/html.test.ts`, `test/suite/board.test.ts`

Logs, probe copies and the memory-sampler log are in `/tmp/claude-1002/-home-zhengyew-telelean/03a29d54-7342-40e3-b5f0-2697a62c93ef/scratchpad/turn2/board-fix/`.

fixed.issue: MAJOR: the board never used the contributed colours. VS Code 1.140 names webview variables "--vscode-" + id.replace(".", "-"), which replaces only the first dot, so telelean.node.formalizedAura became --vscode-telelean-node.formalizedAura while board.css read --vscode-telelean-node-formalizedAura. Same for the kind colours.
fixed.change:
I confirmed the rule in the 1.140 build (workbench.desktop.main.js: `f["vscode-"+v.id.replace(".","-")]`).

1. I renamed the contributed ids in /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/extension/package.json to single-dot ids: telelean.kindAssumption, telelean.kindDerivation, telelean.kindGoal and telelean.formalizedAura. A single-dot id gives the same variable name even if VS Code later replaces every dot.
2. /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/webview/src/styles/board.css now reads var(--vscode-telelean-formalizedAura, var(--vscode-charts-blue)) and the three kind colours the same way. A comment explains the naming rule.
3. Tests:
   - /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/webview/test/shared/vscode-theme.ts encodes VS Code's naming rule and reads the manifest.
   - The new static test /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/webview/test/unit/theme.test.ts checks that every contributed id has one dot, and that board.css (with comments stripped) reads var(<VS Code name>, var(<default>)). It also checks that the CSS uses no telelean variable the manifest does not define.
   - A new Playwright test injects distinctive colours under the names VS Code would derive. It asserts the aura, the legend, the header glyphs and the card stripes.
4. The "rendered" diagnostic now reports the resolved colours: aura, kindA, kindD, kindG and cardAura.
5. A new smoke test sets workbench.colorCustomizations in the test instance's own profile, restores it afterwards, and asserts the colours inside real VS Code. Output: "aura rgb(255, 0, 255), kinds rgb(0, 255, 0) rgb(0, 255, 255) rgb(255, 255, 0) ...; formalised card: rgb(255, 0, 255) 0px 0px 0px 1px, ...".
6. Negative control: with the builder's original ids and CSS names put back in a scratch copy, theme.test.ts gives "Tests  6 failed (6)".

fixed.issue: Minor: CSP violations raised by the HTML document itself (for example a refused stylesheet) were never reported, because the listener attached only when the module bundle ran. Smoke test 2 passed with an unstyled board.
fixed.change:
1. New /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/webview/public/boot.js: a classic script (Vite copies it to dist/webview/boot.js). It listens for securitypolicyviolation from the start, buffers up to 50 violations, and exposes window.__teleleanBoot.drain(sink).
2. reportCspViolations in /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/webview/src/host/bridge.ts forwards the buffer and every later violation. If boot.js did not run, it posts a 'no-boot-script' warning, which the smoke test's "no non-info diagnostics" assertion catches.
3. /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/extension/src/board/html.ts emits `<script nonce src=boot.js>` in head before the stylesheet link; BoardPanel passes bootUri. html.test.ts now checks the two scripts exactly and their order.
4. The "rendered" report gains `styled` (all three lists have overflow-y auto and equal heights). Smoke test 2 asserts styled === true.
5. The harness mirrors the load order. A new negative-control page, test/harness/blocked-style.html, refuses webview.css; its Playwright test asserts a csp-violation (style-src-elem, .../dist/webview.css) is posted before 'ready' and that styled is false.
6. Real VS Code repeat of the verifier's P1c (scratch copy): test 2 now fails with "styled false ... column heights 144,18,36". telelean.log shows "[error] [webview->host] diagnostic {\"level\":\"error\",\"code\":\"csp-violation\",\"message\":\"style-src-elem blocked https://file+.vscode-resource.vscode-cdn.net/.../dist/webview/webview.css\"..." just before "ready".

fixed.issue: Minor: parseWebviewToHost accepted a kindChange with from === to and a theseSuffice with repeated premises; a __proto__ key in diagnostic data was silently dropped.
Minor visual polish: A→G arrows ran through the 'No derivations yet' text; the '▲/▼ n linked' badges covered the first and last visible cards and took their clicks.
fixed.change:
Badges:
- Column.tsx renders an empty slot at the right end of each column header (▲) and in a new 24 px column footer (▼). EdgeEngine owns the button inside each slot (new badgeSlots option) instead of absolutely positioned badges over the board.
- geometry.ts no longer computes badge positions; the BadgeSpec x/y fields are removed and the unit test is updated.
- Column titles truncate with an ellipsis so the buttons stay visible in narrow columns. Buttons are hidden during a drag, when the drop label owns the header.

Empty state: an empty column shows a dashed placeholder with an opaque editor background, vertically centred, so arrows that skip the column pass underneath it as they do under cards.

New Playwright test (badgeReport in helpers.ts): every visible button sits inside its own column's header or footer, covers no visible part of any card, and shows the number of distinct hidden cards its stubs point to. Clicking Goals' ▼ scrolls Goals until the nearest hidden linked card is fully visible, while Assumptions and Derivations keep their scrollTop. The test repeats at 700x520. The Spyro test asserts the placeholder is opaque and centred. The screenshots in /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/webview/test-results/ are regenerated and I viewed them.

fixed.issue: Minor: Chrome cannot start with TMPDIR set to the long scratchpad path ("Socket path too long"), and from /tmp it leaves com.google.Chrome.chrome_chrome_url_fetcher_* folders behind.
Verifier side observation 2 (not listed as an issue): 'rendered' decided it had settled by comparing card counts, so with two graphs in a row it could report from the wrong DOM.
fixed.change:
The store now counts applied graphs (`seq`) and the board carries data-graph-seq. EdgeEngine records the seq it measured (stats.graphSeq), and its MutationObserver also watches that attribute, so a new graph always re-measures. main.tsx waits for measuredSeq === seq. It drops a report whose graph was replaced in the meantime, checking both while polling and in the frame callback that posts. The report data now includes seq and measuredSeq.

A new Playwright test sends two graphs back to back and checks that every report has measuredSeq === seq, a card count matching its own graph, at most one report per graph, and no late report after 2.5 s. With the drop check removed in a scratch copy, it failed 3 out of 3: {"seq":2,"cards":4,...,"measuredSeq":2,"cardsMeasured":75}. That report carried graph #2's label but graph #3's card count.

not_fixed.issue: Old empty /tmp/com.google.Chrome.chrome_chrome_url_fetcher_* folders: 13 in total. 10 are dated 06:58–07:15 today, matching the builder's Playwright runs; 3 are older (2026-10-29 23:11 and two from 2026-11-01 01:45).
not_fixed.reason: I can't prove which process created each one. Under the rule to clean up only what I started, I left them in place; future runs no longer add new ones. They are empty and harmless. To remove them: rmdir /tmp/com.google.Chrome.chrome_chrome_url_fetcher_.*

not_fixed.issue: Verifier side observation 1: 'rendered' is posted before the frame is painted.
not_fixed.reason: A webview has no reliable signal that a frame was presented, because the compositor runs in VS Code's main window. I left the timing as it was and wrote in the reportRendered doc comment that 'rendered' means laid out and drawn into the DOM, not necessarily visible on screen. Later signals that something has settled (for example the M2 review stepper) should not assume it was painted.

not_fixed.issue: Design feedback: the kind and aura colours default to charts.* tokens, and some themes derive those badly. In the real repo's persisted test profile the Goal colour resolves to rgba(238, 238, 238, 0.27).
not_fixed.reason:
That profile is on the Abyss theme (its storage.json has themeBackground #000c18; a fresh profile gets 'Dark 2026', where telelean.kindGoal = --vscode-charts-orange = #cd861a). Abyss does not set charts.orange. In VS Code 1.140 charts.orange falls back to minimap.findMatchHighlight, which falls back to editor.findMatchHighlightBackground, which Abyss sets to #eeeeee44.

The builder's CSS showed the same grey, because it fell back to --vscode-charts-orange, so this is not a regression. Which defaults to use is a design choice (D-15 says theme variables only). Hex defaults per theme type in contributes.colors would avoid it. I don't know how the test profile ended up on Abyss; it is the test instance's profile, not yours.

not_fixed.issue: Deviation from the design doc: 03 section 7 gives `telelean.node.formalizedAura` as the example colour id.
not_fixed.reason: I'm not allowed to edit the design docs. A two-dot id cannot reach a webview under the variable name the CSS can use (only the first dot becomes '-'), so the ids are now telelean.formalizedAura and telelean.kind{Assumption,Derivation,Goal}. Suggested doc note: contributed colour ids must have exactly one dot. theme.test.ts enforces this for future M1 colours.

not_fixed.issue: Disclosure: a temp file landed outside my paths, and a test profile file was created.
not_fixed.reason: Both are already dealt with. A shell slip (`cd X && (...) &` put the cd into the background) ran Playwright once from the repo root. It created /home/zhengyew/telelean/test-results/.last-run.json (created 07:59:52, {"status":"failed","failedTests":[]}). I deleted it, and no other repo file changed in 07:59:40–08:00:10. Separately, my colour smoke test leaves a `{}` settings.json in /home/zhengyew/telelean/packages/extension/.vscode-test/user-data/User/ (the test instance's own profile, gitignored).
